Under development and roadmap

What is built, what is being built, and what comes next, stage by stage. Taken from the build roadmap of the app (updated 2026-11-04) and of the website (updated 2026-11-05).

M0 Foundation — E1 app

4 of 4 stages done

The application as it runs today: projects, 2D sheets with P&ID symbols and lines, attributes, history and undo, floating windows, and Alex in the chat. Every action is one command, used the same way by the interface, Alex, and outside agents, with a local-first AI policy.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
R1-5Refactoring: tests, one domain model, server modules, migrations, the server as the only writerDoneThe code was restructured and covered by tests. The app looks and works as before.
R-FFollow-up: per-user state, frontend structure, typesDonePer-user state and code structure. Nothing new on screen.
6A-6HOne command registry, safe AI edits, local-first AIDone 2026-11-02In the chat, check the mode chip in the header, ask Alex (Agent) to change a sheet, and use Undo on its reply (or turn on "Review changes first" and use Apply / Discard).
6IParity tests, enforcement, and the evaluation set for AI modelsDone 2026-11-02Tests that the interface, Alex, and outside agents run the same commands. Nothing new on screen.

M1 Object model — E1 app

11 of 11 stages doneMVP

Every engineering thing becomes one object with one owner, a class from a versioned library, attributes with sub-attributes and units, and typed relationships to other objects across sections. The library defines how objects behave (where they may live, what they may contain and relate to), and every tool follows the same rules. Tags come from the project's own naming rules. Today's symbols move into signed content packages as records, and every command works object by object, ready for the database of M2.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
M1.0Parity, enforcement, and the evaluation setDone 2026-11-02Parity checks and the AI evaluation set. Nothing new on screen.
M1.0bTest automation pipeline (CI)Done 2026-11-02Every test now runs automatically on each change (GitHub Actions). Nothing new in the app.
M1.1Content packages and the libraryDone 2026-11-02The symbols now come from signed content packages. The symbol picker and the sheets look exactly as before; asking Alex which symbols exist gives the same list.
M1.1bSymbols as content package records, drawn by one renderer (formerly M1.9)Done 2026-11-02Nothing should look different: every symbol is now drawn from its record in the content packages. Open Insert > Asset and page through the types, place a few symbols on a sheet and connect them, and open Model Space: all should look exactly as before.
M1.2Record-level store and the object model migrationDone 2026-11-02Mostly under the hood. Open an existing project: the tree, sheets, and History should look as before, and every edit (and Alex) should still work.
M1.3Content packages visible in project settingsDone 2026-11-02Select a project and choose File > Project settings: its content packages (Core, Electrical foundation, and Plant engineering, which includes instrumentation & control) are listed with versions and what requires each. Ask Alex which content packages the project uses, or what you can place from Plant.
M1.4Tree from ownership, move and delete with previewDone 2026-11-02In the tree, assets appear under Assets, nothing is listed under their sheets, and under each asset its drawings are listed as shortcuts: double-click one to open that drawing with the asset in view. Drag an object to a folder, delete an object and read the preview of what goes with it, then undo through History.
M1.5Classes, attributes, sub-attributes, creating objectsDone 2026-11-02Right-click Assets, choose New asset… and create a Centrifugal pump: its page marks Design pressure and Flow rate as required. Set 10 bar(g), a value under Design pressure / In, and Add attribute; New system… offers no pump.
M1.6Relationships between objectsDone 2026-11-02Create a function under Systems (New system…), and on its Relationships tab choose "is implemented by", pick a pump in the tree and Add: the pump shows under the function. Or drag the pump onto the function with the right mouse button.
M1.7Tags and reference designationsDone 2026-11-02Create a few pumps under Assets without a name: they become P-001, P-002 with the designation -P. Change a pump's short code and see its tag marked out of date; right-click it, Tag…, type a manual tag; then More (…) > Retag… with the preview.
M1.8Tag configuratorDone 2026-11-02Open File > Project settings: under Tag rules, add a rule for pumps (text PU, then the number from 101), watch the sample, Test against project, Save rules, then create a pump under Assets and see it tagged PU-101.

M2 Platform — E1 app

8 of 9 stages doneMVP

E1 moves onto PostgreSQL and into the vendor's cloud. People sign in, belong to organizations, and are invited to projects with roles down to a single section or drawing. Two engineers can work in the same project at the same time without overwriting each other, Alex's proposals are kept safely on the server, and the technical security baseline is in place.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
M2.1PostgreSQL store with the object and history tablesDone 2026-11-03Behind the scenes: with npm run db:up, db:migrate, and db:seed, then E1_STORE=postgres, projects open and edit as before, stored in PostgreSQL tables that keep each organization apart.
M2.2Accounts and sign-inDone 2026-11-03Start npm run dev:identity and the server with E1_AUTH=oidc (README): the sign-in screen appears; the first sign-in claims the installation, a second email gets its own empty workspace.
M2.3Import of existing workspacesDone 2026-11-03Run npm run db:import -- data/db.json, start the server on PostgreSQL, and open it: the tree, sheets, history, and your chat are all there.
M2.4Organizations, invitations, and license tablesDone 2026-11-03On the server with sign-in on, open File > Organization…, invite a colleague by email, open the link signed in as them, and see them listed with their license and the seats used.
M2.5Project permissionsDone 2026-11-03Open a project and choose Members: give a colleague Reviewer; signed in as them, the project opens but moving a symbol is refused with the permission it needs.
M2.6Live refresh, safe saves per object, and stored proposalsDone 2026-11-03Sign in as two people on one project in two browsers: a rename in one appears in the other without reloading; a reply held for review is still there to apply after the server restarts.
M2.7File storageDone 2026-11-03On the server, attach a file to a chat message or upload one to a project, reload the page, and open it again; signed in as someone without a role in the project, it is not found.
M2.8Reference cloud deploymentPlannedOpen E1 from its public cloud address in a normal browser, without installing anything, and sign in.
M2.9Technical security baseline and the M2 gateDone 2026-11-04Mostly under the hood: security settings and checks. You may notice session timeouts and stricter sign-in rules.

M3 Lists and connectivity — E1 app

12 of 12 stages doneMVP

Pipes, cables, wires, and signals become objects connected to ports. Any list is a live table of the model: right-click any node, Query ▸ New query… lists every object below it, in an Excel-like query view that can be filtered, edited, saved as a template (then listed under Query ▸), and exported to Excel. There are no fixed lists. The large 2D drawing editor arrives here. After M3, a first informal pilot preview.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
M3.1The drawing migration: lines as objects, placements in 2DDone 2026-11-04Open a drawn sheet: it looks and edits as before. Under Assets, open Lines: each drawn pipe run, signal, cable, or wire is an object with its own attributes; drawing a second pipe to a nozzle that already has one is refused.
M3.2The 2D sheet viewDone 2026-11-04Open a sheet: the drawing as SVG. Scroll to zoom about the pointer, drag to pan, Fit to see it all, and click a symbol to select it.
M3.3Editing on the 2D viewDone 2026-11-04On a sheet: click and Shift-click to select, drag to move, drag on empty sheet to frame a selection; draw with Connector, add a note with Text, place a symbol from Place symbol…; F flips, Delete deletes, Align lines several up, the grips resize; Pan, Grid, Snap, and Ortho are in the bar.
M3.4Undo, redo, copy, paste, and the editing commandsDone 2026-11-04Undo and redo across the drawing, the tree, and attributes; copy, paste, and duplicate symbols with their tags.
M3.5Query view: read-only tableDone 2026-11-04Right-click a project or section, New query…: a table of the objects below it; click a header to sort, Columns to add attributes.
M3.6Query view: filters, templates, and expressionsDone 2026-11-04Filter with AND/OR/NOT, read the plain-language summary, and save the view as a template for yourself or the project.
M3.7Query view: editing like ExcelDone 2026-11-04Type, paste from Excel, and fill down in the table; one undo restores a whole paste.
M3.8Jobs: spreadsheet export and import with previewDone 2026-11-04Export a table to Excel, change a cell, then Update from Excel…: Check shows exactly that change, Apply makes it.
M3.9Engineering columnsDone 2026-11-04Right-click Assets, Query ▸ New query…; in Columns add Designation and Connects to; Group & totals by Class; save it as your equipment list: it is under Query ▸ from then on. F2 on an owner cell moves the object.
M3.10On the drawing: tags, line numbers, others' changes, layersDone 2026-11-04On a sheet, each symbol shows its tag and each tagged or named run its line number; Layers hides Process, Instrumentation, Electrical, or Annotation on this sheet.
M3.11The 2D view becomes the sheet viewDone 2026-11-04Open any sheet: it is the 2D view, with flow arrows and line crossings, the right-click menus, name labels to drag, formatting, frames, predictive mode, and Layers.
M3.12ISA 5.1 in the Plant packageDone 2026-11-04Open Configuration → Shapes and set Standard to ISA 5.1: every instrument, valve, and logic shape shows its table and number. Place an ISA pressure gauge from the asset window: it is tagged PG-001.

M4 Documents — E1 app

14 of 17 stages doneMVP

Datasheets designed by the users: double-clicking an object opens its datasheet, where values are viewed and edited, and the same layout prints. Revisions and issued documents, PDF of sheets, lists, and datasheets with a title block, Excel import, search, object history, comments, tasks, generated loop diagrams, and Alex's engineering patterns. M4 ends with pilot readiness: access control first (permissions by category, custom roles, objects assigned to a person or group, an exportable access history), then a second cloud, billing, passkeys, and the security and legal reviews a pilot partner needs.

M5 Library lifecycle — E1 app

17 of 17 stages doneMVP

Companies edit and publish their own library: classes, attributes, relationship types, and how they behave. Projects see which updates are available and upgrade with a preview. Equipment catalogs with manufacturer data, a symbol designer with SVG import and live attribute labels, and switching and licensing of content packages.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
11.1Library editor: draft, review, publishDone 2026-11-05Configuration → Company library: make an attribute (a choice of values) and a class that is a kind of Centrifugal pump with that attribute, save them as drafts, publish. The class is then in Object classes, New object offers it, and E1 checks its owners like its own classes.
11.2Updates available, checked against projectsDone 2026-11-05Configuration → Company library: publish a second version of a company class; Updates available in this project lists its objects still on version 1 and what changed. Save a draft that removes a choice or narrows where a class may be owned, and Check against projects lists every object it would break.
11.3Upgrade with previewDone 2026-11-06Publish a new version of a company class, then Configuration → Company library → Preview upgrade: each object is upgraded, has values retired, or is skipped with the reason; Upgrade applies it as one change. A retired value shows with Discard and cannot be edited.
11.4Project library and convention templatesDone 2026-11-06Configuration → Company library: choose This project only and publish a class only this project has. Publish a convention template, Apply to this project, then publish a new version: the project keeps its rules until you apply it again.
20.1Company catalogs and itemsDone 2026-11-06Configuration → Catalogs: create a catalog, add a pump item with manufacturer, model, ordering code and a flow rate, Publish it, then New version, change the flow rate, and Publish again: both versions stay.
20.2Create objects from catalog itemsDone 2026-11-06New asset… on Assets: choose Centrifugal pump, then a catalog item under From catalog. The pump opens with the item's values and From catalog: … above them; change a value and it is marked as differing from the catalog.
20.3Catalog updates, re-apply, replace, detachDone 2026-11-06Publish a new version of a catalog item used by pumps: Company library → Updates available lists it. Re-apply…: a value changed by hand is kept unless ticked; Apply, then Edit → Undo. On a pump, Detach keeps its values.
20.4Project and content package catalogsDone 2026-11-06Configuration → Catalogs: New catalog for This project only, add and publish an item, and make an object from it. Open another project: its catalogs do not list it.
20.5Catalog importDone 2026-11-07Configuration → Catalogs → a catalog → Import…: pick a vendor Excel or CSV list, Dry run to see each row, Import (drafts only), then Publish the drafts. Import the list again after changing one row: only that row becomes a new version.
21.2Symbol designer and publishingDone 2026-11-07Right-click a pump on a sheet → Modify shape…: draw a line in the designer and Save and use here; the pump is drawn with this project's copy. Or Configuration → Shapes → New shape or Derive, then Publish and Allow for a class.
21.3Attribute labels on symbolsDone 2026-11-07Right-click a pump → Modify shape… → Label: choose Design pressure / In, click under the pump, Save and use here. The sheet shows its value; change the value and the label follows; File → Export PDF shows it too.
21.4SVG import into the symbol designerDone 2026-11-08Configuration → Shapes → Import SVG…: choose an SVG of a symbol. The designer opens with a report (what was imported and left out) and two suggested connection points; choose what it draws and Publish.
21.5Symbol versions on placements and upgradeDone 2026-11-08Publish a new version of a company shape: the sheets keep the old one. Configuration → Company library → Updates available lists the shape; Preview placement upgrade, then Upgrade N; one undo takes it back.
01.2bUnits of measurementDone 2026-11-09File → Project settings… → Units: choose Imperial. A new flow rate offers ft³/h first; type only the number. Choose another unit for a value: Convert or Change unit only. (The Model Space 3D view is archived.)
04.2Switching content packages on and offDone 2026-11-09File → Project settings… → Content packages: switch Plant engineering off in a project with pumps: E1 lists what still uses it and keeps it. In an empty project switch it off: New asset… and the symbol picker no longer offer pumps.
04.3Content package licensingDone 2026-11-09File → Organization… → Content packages: which packages your subscription includes and who a per-person package is assigned to. An object of a package that is not licensed is read only, with the reason, and can still be exported.
04.5Content package updatesDone 2026-11-09Configuration → Company library: when E1 ships newer content packages, Updates available lists them per package with what changed. Preview package update, then Update: the project reads the new versions; nothing changes until you take it.

12.6Organization and content package rulesPlannedSee rules that come from your organization or a content package applied in a project.

W2 Hosting and launch — Website

1 of 5 stages doneMVP

The site moves from Netlify to Azure Static Web Apps, lanxtor.com's DNS moves to Azure DNS without breaking mail, and the full site goes live in place of the coming-soon page (docs/AZURE-INTEGRATION.md in Lanxtor/E1Website).

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
W2.1Azure Static Web Apps workflow, coming-soon page, preview siteDone 2026-11-04lanxtor.com shows the coming-soon page; preview.lanxtor.com (password-protected) shows the full site.
W2.2DNS Phase A: lanxtor.com DNS on Azure, mail keptPlanneddig +short NS lanxtor.com shows the Azure nameservers; mail to and from lanxtor.com still works.
W2.3DNS Phase B: www, apex, and app.lanxtor.com on AzurePlannedwww.lanxtor.com and lanxtor.com open from Azure with a certificate; app.lanxtor.com opens the E1 server.
W2.4Netlify retiredPlannedThe Netlify site and DNS zone are deleted; TTLs raised to 3600.
W2.5Launch: the full site on lanxtor.com (SITE_MODE = live)PlannedOpen lanxtor.com: the full site instead of "Coming soon."

W3 Connected to the E1 cloud — Website

1 of 4 stages doneMVP

One account for the app and the website: "Log in" signs in through the E1 server, the account page reads licenses, usage, projects and billing from it, and the Shape E1 board stores posts and votes in E1's PostgreSQL.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
W3.1Website pointed at app.lanxtor.com; account API and board routes on the serverDone 2026-11-04assets/js/config.js points at https://app.lanxtor.com; the server answers /api/account/overview and /api/community/* (server/tests/website.test.mjs).
W3.2Sign-in from the website end to endPlannedOn the website choose Log in, sign in, and land back on the account page with your real license and projects (needs app M2.8, cloud deployment).
W3.3Shape E1 board live on the serverPlannedPost a request on Shape E1 while signed in, reload in another browser: it is there, with its votes.
W3.4Academy courses served by the E1 serverPlannedThe account page lists video courses with your progress and certificates instead of "Video courses are on their way".
